rule: Only claims with status=verified may be published. Every number must be reproducible by the script named in `method`. Wording in `publishable_sentence` is the maximum strength allowed.

claims.claim: Among unique mineral-active baby sunscreen formulations on DailyMed, 49 of 148 (33.1%) contain at least one UV-absorbing excipient not listed as an active ingredient.
claims.publishable_sentence: About 1 in 3 baby sunscreens sold as mineral-only in the US also contain an ingredient that absorbs UV light but is not listed as an active ingredient.
claims.population: category=sunscreen AND baby_labeled=true; deduplicated by formulation_hash (391 registrations -> 332 unique formulations); actives contain ZnO and/or TiO2 and no FDA chemical filter

claims.method: scripts/verify_ledger.py US-HID-001 (independent regex on inactive ingredient names; does NOT use the pipeline flag has_hidden_chemical_filter)

known_limits: baby_labeled classifier also matches company names (e.g. BABYFACE LLC, Baby Bubba soap); excluding the doubtful cases moves the ratio to ~33-34%, sentence unchanged

claims.claim: FDA Final Administrative Order OTC000008-1 (signed 2026-09-08, issued 2026-09-11) amends M020 to remove aminobenzoic acid (PABA) and trolamine salicylate as sunscreen active ingredients, effective 2027-09-11 (or later if disputed).

ingredients.name: butyloctyl salicylate
ingredients.function: Hallstar, a manufacturer, says that at 5% it is responsible for no more than 2 SPF units on its own, that a larger SPF boost can be seen with other filters, and that it can help prevent the breakdown of certain UV filters.

ingredients.name: ethylhexyl methoxycrylene
ingredients.function: Hallstar sells it as SolaStay S1, a photostabilizer, and says it "photostabilizes and improves mineral filter efficacy".

ingredients.name: tridecyl salicylate
ingredients.function: Vantage sells it as JEECHEM TDS, "designed for use as a sunscreen booster", and says it can be combined with titanium dioxide or zinc oxide.

ingredients.name: ethyl ferulate
ingredients.function: Sold as CaribSun UV, which its supplier describes as having "antioxidant, free radical scavenging and UV adsorption properties".

ingredients.name: polyester-8
ingredients.function: Hallstar sells it as Polycrylene, a sunscreen photostabilizer, and lists "SPF Enhancement" as a feature.

ingredients.name: polysilicone-15
ingredients.function: A UV filter in the EU, allowed up to 10% under Annex VI of the EU Cosmetics Regulation. It is not an FDA sunscreen active.

claims.claim: 139 of 446 baby/kids sunscreen formulations list fragrance (or parfum) as an ingredient.
claims.publishable_sentence: 139 of the 446 baby and kids sunscreen formulas listed in the FDA's DailyMed label database list fragrance (or parfum) as an ingredient. For children with eczema, the American Academy of Dermatology advises a sunscreen that is fragrance-free.
claims.legal_framing: Not a violation: fragrance is allowed in US sunscreens. The finding counts what the ingredient lists say; it is not about any brand.
claims.population: unique formulations of sunscreen labels that say baby or kids in the product name or on the front panel, plus the sunscreens of baby-care brands (Tubby Todd, Pipette, Mustela, Babo Botanicals, Babyganics, California Baby, Thinkbaby, Sqween, Putto; tinted and lip products excluded) (FDA DailyMed; selected by rule from the label, with edge cases decided by hand and every decision recorded with its reason; a claim such as 'suitable for children' alone does not count; labels that name a foreign distributor or importer and labels that do not meet US sunscreen limits as listed left out; a listing that bundles several products is split into its products)
